subject: Policy Q&A: residency, retention, and training exclusions
messages:
From: Allison Park <allison.park@finserv.co>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@finserv.co>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs: data residency + training usage

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. Our security review flagged a couple of clarification items around data residency, retention, and specifically whether Redwood ever uses customer content to train models. Can you confirm the following?

1) Do you ever use customer text, prompts, responses, or embeddings to train or fine-tune Redwood models (including internal model improvement pipelines)?
2) Where is customer content stored for the hosted product (region/eu/us)? Are backups/replicas ever copied across regions?
3) What are the retention windows for request/response logs, access logs, and any cached KV/vector artifacts by default?
4) If we request deletion of a customer account, how do you guarantee erasure across backups, snapshots, and third-party processors (e.g., cloud object storage)?

We'd like a short written summary we can pass to our compliance team and ideally a redlined DPA clause that states the "no training" commitment.

Appreciate a short reply and any supporting doc you can attach.

Best,
Allison
Allison Park
Senior Information Security Manager
FinServ Bank

--
Attachment: vendor-security-questionnaire-202607.pdf (the questionnaire PDF we completed)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Park <allison.park@finserv.co>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: data residency + training usage

Hi Allison — thanks for the concise list. Short answers up front, then a few important nuances below. I'm attaching a 1-page retention summary and a DPA/DPA addendum draft for your legal team.

1) Training on customer content: Redwood does NOT use Customer Content from the hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments to train or improve our foundation models or model weights. We also do not feed customer prompts/responses into our public model training pipelines. Any use of customer data for model training would require explicit, documented opt-in and a separate commercial agreement (e.g., custom fine-tune or private evaluation program).

2) Storage & residency: For the hosted product customers can select EU or US data region at onboarding. By default, data stays in the selected region; cross-region replication does not occur except for emergency DR scenarios and only under contractually-approved terms. Dedicated and Private customers control storage location in their environment (VPC/on-prem).

3) Retention windows (defaults):
- Request/response payloads (hosted API): retained 30 days by default for troubleshooting, then deleted.
- Access and audit logs: retained 90 days by default for investigation and billing reconciliation.
- KV cache / ephemeral vectors: by default ephemeral and not persisted beyond the live session; optional caching can be enabled by customers and is then covered by the DPA retention schedule.

4) Deletion & backups:
- Data deletion requests are processed within 72 hours; we issue a deletion confirmation and a summary of affected artifacts.
- Backups/snapshots: encrypted; snapshot lifecycle is 14 days by default for hosted and Dedicated (can be configured for private). We will remove data from backups at the next snapshot rotation and provide attestation. For regulatory or contractual needs we can arrange expedited snapshot purge and certification of erasure.

Additional notes:
- Telemetry and usage metrics: We collect high-level telemetry (error rates, token counts, latency) to operate and improve the service. This telemetry is aggregated and stripped of customer identifiers and is not used to train model weights.
- Third-party processors: we use standard cloud providers (listed in the DPA addendum). We require subprocessors to comply with our DPA and encryption controls.

Next steps: I attached a short PDF summarizing these defaults and a draft Data Processing Addendum clause that includes the explicit "no training without consent" sentence. If that looks good, Marissa (legal) and Soojin (privacy) are copied here to work through any redlines.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_data_retention_summary_20260809.pdf, data_processing_addendum_draft.docx

From: Allison Park <allison.park@finserv.co>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: data residency + training usage

Thanks Hannah — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our legal & infra folks:

- We need explicit language for backups and snapshots: will customer content remain in any long-term archival storage beyond the 14-day snapshot lifecycle you mentioned? Are snapshots ever copied to a separate cold storage tier?
- For hosted EU customers: are there any subprocessors (e.g., analytics, monitoring) that are outside the EU and have access to plaintext content?
- Embeddings / vector stores: does Redwood persist embeddings or any derived model artifacts by default? If persisted, where and for how long?

If you can include the exact line we'd add to the DPA and any proposed SLA text about deletion timelines, that would speed our review.

Best,
Allison

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Park <allison.park@finserv.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: data residency + training usage

Allison — looping in Marissa (legal) and Soojin (privacy) to confirm contractual language and subprocessors. Below are exact, customer-ready clauses and clarifications we can insert into the DPA and operational SLA. Please let us know if you'd prefer this as a redline.

Proposed DPA clause (no-training):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content, Customer-provided training data, or any customer-derived embeddings to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's models or model weights without the Customer's explicit, documented opt-in. This prohibition applies to all Redwood-managed model training pipelines and any third-party model training services engaged by Redwood."

Backups & snapshots:
- Default lifecycle: hosted snapshots are retained for 14 days and only copied to cold archival storage in exceptional DR cases; cold archival storage is encrypted with customer-segregated keys where required by contract.
- Expedited purge: if a customer requests immediate deletion for regulatory reasons, Redwood will coordinate an expedited purge and provide an attestation of removal from active backups within a contractual timeframe (typical turnaround: 10 business days for complete removal from archives).

Subprocessors & cross-region access:
- For EU-region hosted customers, no subprocessors requiring access to plaintext Customer Content are based outside the EU by default. Monitoring/telemetry agents transmit aggregated metrics only. Any exception is listed in our DPA subprocessor appendix and requires prior notice.

Embeddings/vector artifacts:
- Default: Redwood does not persist vector indexes derived from Customer Content unless a customer enables long-term caching or index storage (e.g., for retrieval-augmented generation). If enabled, the location and retention of those artifacts follow the customer's selected data region and the DPA retention schedule.

SLA language (suggested):
"Redwood will acknowledge and initiate Customer Content deletion requests within 72 hours and will provide confirmation of removal from active systems within 72 hours. Removal from backups and archives will be completed within the timeframe specified in the Data Processing Addendum (standard: 10 business days for archival purge)."

Action items:
1) Marissa — can you attach a redline of the DPA with the proposed clause above?
2) Soojin — please confirm subprocessors list and whether we need to provide a subprocessor map for FinServ.
3) Allison — happy to set a 30-minute call if your team wants to walk through the draft.

Thanks — Hannah
